topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
consensus_response: Frequency planning must address both physical and system-level interference.  Satellite Uplink frequencies are susceptible to co-channel interference from PLCs, requiring minimum spacing (50 MHz) and exclusion zones. Dynamic frequency allocation techniques, adaptive modulation schemes (OFDM/QAM), and real-time weather data integration enhance spectrum efficiency and mitigate interferences caused by changing signal propagation conditions. These strategies ensure both satellite and PLC networks coexist efficiently while minimizing interference.
reference_context: The availability of radio spectrum is limited.  To maximize spectral efficiency, satellite internet providers and terrestrial networks can share the same frequencies for reuse. This shared frequency usage requires strict coordination between operators to prevent interference from occurring.
